guardrails.title: Never trust a client-supplied tenant id
guardrails.description: Every feature row is partitioned PK = TENANT#{principal.tenant_id}. Derive the tenant from the principal, never from the request body or a query string.

guardrails.title: Mutating endpoints require a role check
guardrails.description: Call require_role(principal, 'editor') or 'admin' before any write. Read endpoints do not.

guardrails.title: API keys must be sent as Authorization: Bearer
guardrails.description: The gateway authoriser only reads the Authorization header. An X-API-Key-only request is rejected before it reaches a handler.

guardrails.title: Compose class names with cn()
guardrails.description: Import cn() from @systemdox/utils rather than concatenating template strings.

spec-preferences.name: User preferences endpoint
spec-preferences.proposalContent: Console users need per-user preferences (theme, default project, digest cadence) that survive across devices. This spec adds a REST endpoint under /v1/preferences on the systemdox-backend-prod stack.
spec-preferences.taskContent:
1. Add the prefs_api handler.
2. Register GET/PUT routes in template.yaml.
3. Add a typed BaseApiService subclass in the console app.

requirements.name: REQ-1 Tenancy
requirements.content: Preference rows MUST be keyed PK = TENANT#{tenant_id}, SK = PREF#{user_sub}. The handler MUST call resolve_principal(event) and derive the key with tenant_pk(principal). A client-supplied tenant id MUST be rejected.

requirements.name: REQ-2 Authorisation
requirements.content: GET /v1/preferences MUST be readable by any authenticated member. PUT /v1/preferences MUST call require_role(principal, 'editor'). Requests MUST carry Authorization: Bearer <key>.

spec-notifications.name: Notifications feature
spec-notifications.proposalContent: In-app notifications for staleness alerts and publish failures. Specs follow the shared-specs convention: RFC 2119 keywords (MUST/SHOULD/MAY) and Given/When/Then scenarios.

requirements.name: REQ-1 Delivery
requirements.content: Given a publish failure, When the worker exhausts its retries, Then a notification MUST be written to the tenant's notification feed. Notifications SHOULD be deduplicated by job id.

items.title: ADR-022: Host the MCP server as a Lambda

doc-db-design.content:
# Database design

All feature data lives in one DynamoDB table, partitioned by tenant.

## Keys

- `PK = TENANT#{principal.tenant_id}` — never `USER#`, never a client-supplied value.
- `SK` names the entity: `SPEC#{id}`, `DOC#{id}`, `PREF#{user_sub}`.

Use `tenant_pk(principal)` to build the partition key and `assert_tenant_owns(principal, item)` for items keyed by a bare id (jobs, agent sessions). Attribution goes in `createdBy` / `updatedBy` attributes, never in the key.

## Migrations

Re-keying rows (for example the 2026-07 org rename) runs as a one-shot workflow that scans the table, rewrites `PK`, and is safe to re-run: rows already carrying the new key are skipped.

doc-auth.content:
# Authentication and authorisation

Every handler starts with `principal = resolve_principal(event)`. The principal carries `tenant_id`, `sub`, and `role`.

## API keys

The shared PwebAuthoriser accepts a Cognito JWT or a SystemDox API key. Keys MUST be presented as `Authorization: Bearer pweb_prod_key_...`; an `X-API-Key`-only request is rejected at the gateway with a 401 before the handler runs.

## Roles

`require_role(principal, 'editor')` on every mutating endpoint; `'admin'` for tenant settings. Read endpoints do not call it.

doc-adr-022.content:
# ADR-022: Host the MCP server as a Lambda

## Context

The MCP server (`packages/mcp-server`) can run locally over stdio, but evaluators will not install anything.

## Decision

Deploy `src/http.ts` as a Lambda behind `{tenant}.mcp.systemdox.com/mcp`, speaking stateless Streamable HTTP. Tool registration is shared with the stdio entry point via `createServer()` in `src/server.ts`, so a new tool is registered exactly once and both transports get it.

## Consequences

A new tool means: a `register*` function in `src/tools/`, a line in `createServer`, and a bump to the tool count asserted by `smoke-http.mjs`.

doc-docs-publishing.content:
# Docs publishing pipeline

Published tenant docs are static Starlight sites served at `{tenant}.document.systemdox.com`.

The publish worker renders the tenant's documents with the template in `backend/layers/common/common/docs_template.py` and uploads them to S3 behind the docs-portal CloudFront distribution.

**Bump `TEMPLATE_VERSION_BASE` whenever the template changes what published sites render** — `rebuild-all-docs` enqueues without `force`, so the worker's no-change guard silently skips every site otherwise.

Publishing without a `PUBLISH_CONFIG` orphans the site from the reconcile loop; repairing one means restoring the manifest, the S3 prefix, the `_content/` tree, and the search embedding.

doc-backend-routes.content:
# Adding a backend route

A route exists in two places and both must agree:

1. The handler's own router (`backend/functions/<name>/app.py`).
2. The `Events` block of the function in `backend/template.yaml`.

A route wired in the handler but missing from `template.yaml` produces a CORS preflight 403 from the console — the request never reaches Lambda. A guard test walks the handler's routes and asserts each one appears in the template.

Two functions declaring the same method+path fail the deploy at CloudFormation time, not at build time: `sam validate` will not catch it.

doc-frontend-services.content:
# Frontend API services

Console API calls go through a typed service that extends `BaseApiService` (`apps/app/src/services/`). The base class injects the Cognito token, prefixes the `/systemdox` base path, and normalises errors into the `SYD` error-code space.

Do not call `axios` directly from a component.

doc-header.content:
# The cross-surface console header

The header is rendered twice: once by React (`apps/app`) and once by the Starlight docs template. The two must stay in visual lockstep — a source-level guard (`headerParity.test.ts`) and a Playwright visual spec compare them at four breakpoints and both themes.

Note that in `apps/app`, Tailwind's `dark:` variant follows `prefers-color-scheme`, NOT a `.dark` class. Toggling a `.dark` class half-works and looks like a bug.

rules.text: Use resolve_principal(event) for identity in every handler.
Type hints on every Python function.
Functional React components; CVA variants for shared UI.
Specs use RFC 2119 keywords and Given/When/Then scenarios.
